Prevention: Maize seed to prevent introduction of weed
Avoid grazing animals in affected areas to prevent spread of seeds and plant fragments and poisoning of the animals
Use clean machines and clean water source for irrigation to prevent weed seed spread
Prevent runoff water from infested land into clean fields by making cutoff drains
Maintain a regular weeding regime in crops (general crop sanitation)
Top dress with nitrogen to boost maize health
Use properly decomposted manure to avoid introduction of weeds
Intercrop with cover crops such as
Dolichos lablab, cowpeas and beans to cover the soil
Monitoring: Annual succulent herb with tap root, common in annual and perennial crops at the roadside ans on wasteland.
Plants are reddish in colour, up to 50cm tall, stems are prostrate, round and hairless; can form dense mats.
Leaves thick (2-3cm long) and smooth, clustered at the end of branches.
Fruit capsule (4-8mm) containing many small oval, black seeds.
Propagated by seed and stem fragments
Regularly check the farm for small plant fragments and plantlets; control to prevent establishment
Direct Control: Uproot plants or remove flowering stems before flowering to prevent seed set
Deeply bury the weed in a pit (approx 1m deep) to prevent future spread
Linuron (1.5kg/ha) for pre- emergence control of the weed
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance
Board (PCPB) for registered list of availed herbicides
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Use 2,4-D amine salt post emergence to control the weed in maize monocrop (2L/ha).
Apply once at 3 - 4 weed leaf stage.
If rains continue and more weeds grow then a second application is necessary
Apply once at pre emergence stage (weed and crop).
Planting of other crops such as beans will be restricted (6 months).
Bentazon can be used if maize is intercroppped with beans as a broad application or glyphosate for spot treatment of patches
